newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes higher on inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes higher on inflows.

text.p: *Central Bank not intervening in the market
Inflows from portfolio investments and overseas workers remittances propped up the Philippine peso which closed at 26.267 on Friday from 26.275, traders said.
The day's average was at 26.272 versus 26.277, with volume rising to $110.68 million from $88.50 million.
"The absence of demand from commercials also created the scenario for a stronger peso," a trader from a big bank said.
News that the trade deficit widened by 42.5 percent to $9.132 billion failed to weaken the peso due to strong dollar inflows, traders said.
"The Central Bank has consistently reiterated the trade deficit was not alarming," said the same dealer.
For the third straight day, the Central Bank stayed out of the market but it trended its desired trading range in line with the strengthening of the peso.
It changed its bid and quote for the dollar at 26.22 and 26.27 respectively versus the previous 26.235 and 26.285, traders said.
Traders predict the peso could be stronger next week.
